analyst_observations.observation: The skill's biggest value is in STRUCTURAL COMPLIANCE. All 5 baseline failures were about format/location, not content quality. Without the skill, agents produce good content but in wrong formats (.md vs .mmd, flat directories vs proper paths, [HH:MM] placeholder vs real time).

ACCESS CHAIN is the most discriminating assertion. The with_skill agent always started from CLAUDE.md → documentation/ → ~/.quack/brain/. The baseline skipped CLAUDE.md entirely and mixed code exploration with brain search.

The skill SAVES tokens overall (-15.4% average). Despite the skill itself adding ~200 lines to context, it provides clearer instructions that reduce exploration. The baseline spent more tokens 'figuring out' the correct format by reading existing files.
The skill adds ~6.8% to execution time on average. This is a small cost for 100% compliance vs 63% without. The time delta is mostly from the skill agent reading the SKILL.md file itself.

Content quality assertions (has_yaml_frontmatter, presents_summary, diary_correct_author) pass equally in both configurations. The baseline agent infers correct frontmatter by reading existing files — the skill's value is NOT in teaching YAML frontmatter but in teaching the SPECIFIC conventions (file extensions, directory structure, access chain order).

The with_skill agent consistently produced EXTRAS that the baseline didn't: Brain breadcrumbs in code, brand colors in diagrams, references to related entries, preserved existing diary entries instead of creating standalone files.
